subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What public API shape should OpenClaw expose for Telegram custom emoji entities in shared message-tool sends, captions, edits, and replies?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding raw `entities`, Telegram-specific `channelData`, or a portable rich-text/custom-emoji span changes the public message-tool/plugin boundary and fallback semantics.

options.title: Define entity-bearing message API
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved entity representation and implement it consistently across message-tool, Telegram send/edit/caption/reply delivery, and tests.

options.title: Keep raw HTML and richMessages only
options.body: Treat `<tg-emoji>` HTML and Bot API rich messages as the supported path while accepting that user-supplied entity arrays remain unsupported.

options.title: Split design from implementation
options.body: Designate a narrower API-design item first, then implement only after the public contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Define entity-bearing message API
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved entity representation and implement it consistently across message-tool, Telegram send/edit/caption/reply delivery, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing discussion and current-file history make steipete the best available routing candidate for this API-shape choice.
